What is an Add-on?

An Add-on is an optional, explicitly enabled extension to the pipeline. Add-ons introduce additional behavior or coordination capabilities that are not part of the core pipeline and therefore must be declared during FeatureCell configuration.

In practice, an Add-on is most commonly a Behavior that is not included in the core pipeline. Unlike core functionality, Add-ons never execute unless they are explicitly registered in the FeatureCell definition.

Add-ons are never implicitly enabled. If an Add-on is not included in the FeatureCell declaration, it does not participate in pipeline execution and has no effect on state, control flow, or snapshots.

When a FeatureCell is configured, validates each registered Add-on and integrates it into the pipeline at its declared execution boundary. Add-ons do not alter pipeline structure, ordering, or core behavior; they operate strictly within their declared contracts.

This model ensures that all non-core capabilities are explicit, opt-in, and auditable, allowing FeatureCells to remain minimal by default while supporting targeted extension when required.

Add-on Anatomy

Every Add-on behavior conforms to the same structural and contractual requirements as the construct it extends.

Because all Add-ons conform to established contracts, they integrate safely into the pipeline without requiring special handling or awareness from other pipeline participants.

Core Functionality vs Add-ons

distinguishes clearly between core pipeline functionality and Add-ons.

Core Pipeline

  • Always present and guaranteed for every FeatureCell.
  • Responsible for scheduling, input resolution, state progression, and snapshot emission.
  • Cannot be disabled, replaced, or reordered.

Add-ons

  • Optional, engineer-selected extensions.
  • Must be explicitly included in the FeatureCell declaration.
  • May be sourced from extension packages (such as /addons) or implemented directly by engineers.
  • Provide non-core capabilities such as filtering, taps, stepwise policy enforcement, persistence, instrumentation, or coordination.
  • Execute only within their declared boundaries and must not violate pipeline contracts.

This separation ensures a stable, predictable core while allowing FeatureCells to opt into additional behavior only when explicitly required.

Why Add-ons Matter

Add-ons are the mechanism by which FeatureCells remain both minimal and extensible:

  • Explicit — All non-core behavior is declared, visible, and reviewable.
  • Composable — FeatureCells are extended by adding Add-ons, not by modifying core logic.
  • Deterministic — Add-ons execute only at defined stages with clear contracts.
  • Safe — Core pipeline guarantees remain intact regardless of which Add-ons are enabled.

Understanding Add-ons is essential to understanding how balances extensibility with deterministic pipeline execution.

Pipeline

Add-ons do not alter the pipeline lifecycle. Instead, they occupy well-defined execution slots within it. Pipeline ordering remains deterministic regardless of which Add-ons are enabled.

Simplified Execution Flow

Example FeatureCell Declaration 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell<Employee[]>(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [],
  },
  [
    // opt-in behavior array 
    withLookupBehavior
  ],
  [
    // opt-in controller array 
  ]
);

// Apply debounce during initialization
employeeCell
  .withLookup?.({
    idKey: 'id',
    fetchType: ResolveTypes.Promise,
    fetch: (id: string) => promise 
  })
.initialize();`}}
